name: A320neo-era livery
description: White fuselage, the aft third navy behind a straight diagonal rising from the belly behind the wing to the fin's leading edge. Navy fin with the Aegean bird: two white crescent feathers sweeping up to the trailing edge, with pale blue extensions below them. Navy engines. 'AEGEAN' in spaced navy capitals above the forward windows, 'aegeanair.com' over the rear windows.

Re-checked 2026-11-15: this is an A320neo (the 'A320neo' mark by the door), not an A321neo; fitted to the measured A320 shape (doors pinned, camera 6° below): titles and the diagonal measured on it.

navy.name: Aegean blue (a deep blue that reads blue in sun and overcast, never black)

areas.name: pale blue sliver ahead of the navy's diagonal
navy aft section behind a diagonal
the forward pale stroke carried on from the fin's root down across the tail cone, under the tailplane, to a point low on the side
pale blue stroke under the upper feather, from its point down to the fin's root
pale blue stroke under the lower feather, narrowing down the rudder to the root
upper white feather, from the tip's trailing corner sweeping down and forward to a point

logos.description: Small Star Alliance star by the forward door.

titles.style: Widely spaced, wide geometric capitals of medium-bold weight above the forward windows.
Small lower-case web address over the rear windows, ahead of the navy.

notes: The Aegean bird is drawn as fin areas only (a logo entry as well had renderers draw it twice, the two never lining up): two white crescent feathers sweeping up and aft to the trailing edge, cut square on one level line, each going on below it in pale blue curving the other way, an S. When the scheme was introduced isn't dated here; it came with the A320neo family deliveries. The earlier scheme (white with a navy-and-blue fin) remains on A320ceo-family aircraft; not drawn. Belly under the forward fuselage white; aft navy. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on SX-NEB (A320neo, fitted to the A320 shape): 'AEGEAN' sits right on the window tops (y 0.28, it had floated higher), x 0.164-0.37; 'aegeanair.com' x 0.673-0.757; the diagonal agrees (reduced to its ends); the feathers drawn as curves. Re-measured 2026-11-27 on SX-NEE (left) and SX-NEK (right): the pale blue strokes were drawn leaning the wrong way; they curve down and aft as the feathers' S, the upper one running on over the tail cone; a pale blue sliver ahead of the navy's diagonal added. Dark colours checked in sun (SX-NET, 2025-05-01): the fin, the aft block, the engines and the titles are one navy, which reads blue, not black. Reconciled 2026-11-27 with a trace off SX-NAD (A321neo, right side, sharp and square on, fitted to the A21N shape, tools/photo_trace.py): the bird's feathers and pale strokes are those traced curves, in fin space, so the one set fits the A320neo and the A321neo alike (their fins are the same and the art sits the same on SX-NEE, SX-NEK and SX-NAD); SX-NEE's measure had the upper feather a little narrower than SX-NAD shows it. The forward pale stroke on the tail cone is SX-NAD's trace too. Still no logo entry: the areas are the bird. Colours re-sampled on SX-NAD in sun and in low light: the blue #142665-#252F6A, a deep blue (#1A2766) a little lighter and bluer than it was; the pale strokes #909EB8-#97A6BD (#97A7C1).
